subject.title: fix: Teams Graph and media work with RFC2544 proxy DNS

question: Should the Teams plugin accept RFC2544 fake-IP DNS results for its explicit Graph and approved media hostname policies after the contributor supplies real proxy-DNS evidence?
rationale: The code deliberately relaxes a shared SSRF safety classification for a deployment-specific network topology; maintainers must confirm that this scoped compatibility boundary is the intended product and security policy.

options.title: Require live proxy-DNS proof, then accept the narrow exception
options.body: Have the contributor provide redacted after-fix Graph and media guarded-fetch evidence from an RFC2544 fake-IP proxy setup, including confirmation that unrelated private targets remain blocked.

options.title: Keep the existing strict block
options.body: Decline the exception if the repository should not support host-proxied fake-IP DNS for Teams-managed outbound requests.

recommendation.title: Require live proxy-DNS proof, then accept the narrow exception
recommendation.body: Have the contributor provide redacted after-fix Graph and media guarded-fetch evidence from an RFC2544 fake-IP proxy setup, including confirmation that unrelated private targets remain blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent scoped RFC2544 SSRF-policy work makes this account the best available low-confidence routing candidate for the boundary decision.
